question: Smith Rock/Broughton pairs: (a) Red Eye (3 pitches) vs Red Eye [E] (1 pitch, 18 m) on Broughton Red Wall - one climb or two? (b) Chouinard's Crack (1st Half Pitch of Peking) vs Peking - merge or keep both?
answer: (a) Mountain Project's Red Wall area (22 climbs) holds exactly ONE Red Eye entry, 'Red Eye [E]', sport 5.10; the area page lists no second Red Eye. So our two rows are one climb. Our 'Red Eye' row carries the 3-pitch count and an overview describing a bolted first pitch, then a crack and an offwidth corner; the [E] row has the 1-pitch/18 m numbers. A mirror (OpenBeta) calls it a popular 5.10 with unknown FA and a roughly 60 ft first anchor stage, which fits pitch 1 being the sport pitch. (b) Mountain Project's Red Wall (Smith) area lists BOTH 'Peking' (trad, 5.9-) and 'Chouinard's Crack (1st Half Pitch of Peking)' (trad/TR, 5.9-) as separate climbs. Peking is two pitches (crux finger crack on pitch 1, easy pitch 2); Chouinard's Crack is that splitter climbed as a stand-alone single pitch or top rope. They share a start, but the crack is logged on its own.
recommendation: (a) MERGE or_red_wall_red_eye_e into or_red_eye_2 (keep or_red_eye_2: it holds the overview and pitch count; sport 5.10; name 'Red Eye', the [E] tag is the listing's marker, not part of the name; the 18 m length belongs to pitch 1 only). (b) KEEP BOTH: Chouinard's Crack is a recognised stand-alone climb listed separately. Optionally set Peking pitches to 2 (sources say two; our row says 3).

b.note: Peking pitch count 2 per two sources vs our 3
